Sefton's population increased by around 5,400 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population reached nearly 280,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Sefton increased by 2.0%, from around 273,800 in 2011 to around 279,200 in 2021.

The population here increased by a smaller percentage than the overall population of the North West (5.2%), and by a smaller percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Sefton was home to around 12.7 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 12.5 in 2011. This area was among the top 35% most densely populated English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was lower in Sefton than across the North West

An older Sefton

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Sefton increased by two years, from 44 to 46 years of age.

This area had a higher average (median) age than the North West as a whole in 2021 (40 years) and a higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by just over 5,100 (an increase of 9.0%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by around 6,200 (11.3% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 1.4 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Disability in Sefton

In 2021, 9.9% of Sefton residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 11.2% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just under one in nine people (10.7%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 10.5% in 2011. The proportion of Sefton residents who were not disabled increased from 78.3% to 79.3%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot was greater across the North West (2.1 percentage points, from 11.2% to 9.1%) than in Sefton (1.3 percentage points). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Sefton decreased by 1.3 percentage points

Rise in private renting

Of Sefton households, 18.2% rented privately in 2021, up from 13.4% in 2011.

The increase in the percentage of privately-rented homes was greater in Sefton (4.8 percentage points) than across the North West (3.9 percentage points, from 15.4% to 19.2%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.6 percentage points, from 16.8% to 20.5%.

Private renting in Sefton increased by 4.8 percentage points

Unpaid care in Sefton

In 2021, 4.9% of Sefton residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.8% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just under 1 in 40 people (2.4%) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 1.9% in 2011. The proportion of Sefton residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care remained at 3.4%.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Sefton (2.9 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the North West (2.7 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.5%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Sefton decreased by 2.9 percentage points

Religion in Sefton

In 2021, 28.6% of Sefton residents reported having "No religion", up from 15.8% in 2011. The rise of 12.8 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Sefton. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the North West, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 19.8% to 32.6%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 64.4% of people in Sefton described themselves as Christian (down from 76.8%), while 5.0% did not state their religion (down from 6.2% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Sefton residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 255,200 Sefton residents said they were born in England. This represented 91.4% of the local population. The figure has decreased from just over 255,600 in 2011, which at the time represented 93.4% of Sefton's population.

Scotland was the next most represented, with around 2,800 Sefton residents reporting this country of birth (1.0%). This figure was down from just over 3,200 in 2011, which at the time represented 1.2% of the population of Sefton.

The number of Sefton residents born in Poland rose from just over 1,600 in 2011 (0.6% of the local population) to around 2,600 in 2021 (0.9%).

In 2021, 91.4% of Sefton residents reported their country of birth as England

Health in Sefton

In 2021, 48.4% of Sefton residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 46.2% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 32.6% to 31.9%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Sefton residents describing their health as "very bad" remained 1.5%, while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 5.4% to 4.9%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

In 2021, 1.5% of usual residents said their health was very bad in Sefton

National identity in Sefton

In 2021, 4.3% of Sefton residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 2.5% in 2011.

In 2021, 0.8% of residents identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 0.3% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Sefton that identified as "British only" increased from 15.0% to 61.8%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater across the North West (2.3 percentage points, from 4.7% to 7.1%) than in Sefton (1.8 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Sefton increased by 1.8 percentage points

Family in Sefton

In 2021, 14.4% of Sefton households included a couple but no children. This figure decreased from 14.8% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in six households (16.0%) included a couple with dependent children, compared with 17.2% in 2011. The percentage of single family households including a couple living with only non-dependent children decreased from 8.0% to 7.7%.

The decrease in the percentage of households including a couple but no children in Sefton (0.4 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the North West (0.5 percentage points, from 16.5% to 16.0%). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.9 percentage points, from 17.6% to 16.8%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in Sefton decreased by 0.4 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Sefton residents aged 16 years and over, 37.3% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 33.1% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 4 in 10 people (43.0%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 46.2% in 2011. The percentage of adults in Sefton that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership increased from 9.3% to 9.7%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership was greater in Sefton (4.2 percentage points) than across the North West (3.8 percentage points, from 35.6% to 39.4%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Sefton increased by 4.2 percentage points

Employment in Sefton

Of Sefton residents aged 16 years and over, 52.2% said they were employed (excluding full-time students) in 2021, a similar percentage as in 2011 (52.1%).

In 2021, just over 1 in 40 people (2.6%) said they were unemployed, compared with 4.3% in 2011. The percentage of retired Sefton residents decreased from 26.8% to 26.6%.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed fell from 54.2% to 53.7% across the North West. Across England, the percentage fell from 56.5% to 55.7%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Sefton increased by 0.2 percentage points

Working hours in Sefton

In 2021, 9.8% of Sefton residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure was at a similar level in 2011 (9.6%).

In 2021, around 1 in 11 people (9.0%) said they worked over 49 hours per week, compared with 10.7% in 2011. The percentage of adults in employment working 31 to 48 hours per week increased from 57.6% to 59.6%.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week increased from 9.1% to 9.6% across the North West. Across England, the percentage increased from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Sefton increased by 0.2 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Sefton

In 2021, 1.5% of Sefton residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 1.0% in 2011. The 0.5 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the North West, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 6.2% to 8.4%, while across England the percentage increased from 7.8% to 9.6%.

In 2021, 95.8% of people in Sefton identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 97.4% in 2011), while 1.5% identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category (compared with 1.0% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group") increased from 0.3% in 2011 to 0.7% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.
